system.description:
A slender rod of blackened ash, warm to the touch when a spell is on the wielder's lips. It has the following Powers:

  • (+1) Trinket: Deals an extra +1 Spell damage, and the wielder ignores half-Cover when Casting.

Taken from the warden's quarters at Revel's End, where it was used far more often than the paperwork admits. It has the following Powers:

  • Binding: Holds 3 charges, all of which return after a Rest. Expend a charge to Restrain a Being you can see within Near ([Might] negates, repeatable at the end of each of its Turns), or to immediately end a Restrained or Grappling Status on yourself.
  • Entangle: A Being Restrained by the wand is Vulnerable for as long as it stays Restrained.

Vellynne Harpell keeps one on her belt and reaches for it more readily than she admits. It has the following Powers:

  • Magic Missile: Holds 3 charges, all of which return after a Rest. Expend a charge to send three darts of force at Beings you can see within Far, dealing 1d4+1 damage each. The darts never miss. Spend up to 3 further charges to send one extra dart each.

A skull-topped rod of the Demon Prince of Undeath. The one in the White Wyrm's hoard is a replica - though nothing about holding it feels like a replica. It has the following Powers:

  • (+3) Weapon: Deals an extra +3 damage.
  • Soul Eater: Those killed by it can't be resurrected unless a wish is granted to do so.
  • Vicious: On a Crit, the Target takes extra damage equal to twice its HD.
  • Bane of the Living: Deals an extra damage die to the living; Undead who see it must pass [Will] or serve the wielder.
  • Doom: The wielder only regains 1 HP per die rolled to heal them, and Undead everywhere become aware of where the wand is.

Duergar looted it from a drow caravan and never worked out how to stop it sticking to things. It has the following Powers:

  • Webbing: Holds 3 charges, all of which return after a Rest. Expend a charge to fill a Near Cube with thick webbing: it is Difficult Terrain, and a Being that enters it or starts its Turn in it must pass [Reflex] or be Restrained.
  • Entangle: A Being Restrained by the webs is Vulnerable until it breaks free.

Recovered from Drakareth's Doom, still faintly warm from whatever the wraith was doing with it. It has the following Powers:

  • Charming: Holds 5 charges, all of which return after a Rest. Expend a charge to Cast Charm. As a Reaction to an enchantment Spell targeting you, absorb it instead and regain a charge.
  • Repulsing: The wielder has Favor on Saves against the Charmed Status.

Avarice keeps it close, and the cold that clings to it is noticeably worse than the weather outside. It has the following Powers:

  • (+2) Trinket: Deals an extra +2 damage with Cold Spells.
  • Resistance: Favor on Saves and damage reduction against Cold.
  • Winter's Reach: Holds 5 charges, all of which return after a Rest. Expend a charge to Cast Freeze or Frostburn. If it is broken while empty, it melts into water.

One of Iriolarthas's own, and still the single most dangerous thing a character can pick up in Ythryn. It has the following Powers:

  • (+2) Trinket: Deals an extra +2 Spell damage.
  • (+2) Armor: +2 bonus to Armor while the staff is held.
  • (+2) Protection: +2 bonus to Saves while the staff is held.
  • Force Bolt: Expend a charge to strike a Being within Far with a bolt of force for 5d6 damage, or swing the staff in melee for an extra 1d6.
  • Retributive Strike: Holds 5 charges, all of which return after a Rest. Break the staff to release its remaining power in a Far Sphere for 16d6 damage, halved by distance. The wielder is destroyed.

A band of bronze cast as a curled ram's head, found in the wreck of a Netherese skycoach. It has the following Powers:

  • Ram's Charge: Holds 3 charges, all of which return after a Rest. Expend a charge to strike a Being within Far with a spectral ram: 2d10 damage and shoved 15 feet.

Worth more than gold on the Eastside of Termalaine, and everybody there knows it. It has the following Powers:

  • Resistance: Favor on Saves and damage reduction against Cold. The wearer is unharmed by Blistering Cold.

Pried out of a shipwreck frozen into the ice off Solstice. It has the following Powers:

  • (+2) Weapon: Deals an extra +2 damage.

Vassavicken's axe. It wants to be swung, and it is not especially concerned at what. It has the following Powers:

  • (+2) Weapon: Deals an extra +2 damage.
  • (+1) Armor: +1 bonus to Armor while the axe is carried.
  • Anger: The wielder always fails Saves against Berserk. While Berserk they must Attack the nearest Being each Turn, and cannot willingly part with the axe.

Dwarven-made and light as cloth, it never announces the wearer the way steel does. It has the following Powers:

  • Featherweight: Counts as Chain armor, but never imposes Hinder on Checks to move quietly and has no Might requirement.

A ceramic jug that produces whatever it feels like producing, within reason. It has the following Powers:

  • Endless Draught: Once per Rest, name a liquid - water, ale, oil, honey, vinegar, wine, or mayonnaise - and the jug fills with it.

Found in the Black Cabin, where Macreadus apparently valued it less than his machine. It has the following Powers:

  • Vigour: The wearer's Might score becomes 19 if it isn't already higher.

Perfectly ordinary beans. That is the problem. It has the following Powers:

  • Sprouting: Plant a bean and something happens - a treant, a geyser, a rain of toads, or a small, extremely angry monster. Roll on the DM's table.

Confiscated from Dzaan by the Easthaven militia and never entered into evidence. It has the following Powers:

  • Menagerie: Reach in and pull out a fuzzy object, which becomes a random Beast that obeys you. Three uses, which return after a Rest.

Hilda's thanks for bringing her children home. It has the following Powers:

  • Resistance: Favor on Saves and damage reduction against Cold; the wearer is unharmed by Blistering Cold.
  • Snowstrider: Ice and deep snow are never Difficult Terrain for the wearer.

A hollow mithral tube that Netherese librarians used instead of keys. It has the following Powers:

  • Opening: Strike the chime to Cast Knock on one object within Near. Three uses, after which the chime cracks and is spent.

The wearer is easy to overlook, and the cloak's colour never quite settles. It has the following Powers:

  • Invisibility I: While the hood is up, skip your Move to become Invisible until after you take an Action. Beings have Hinder on Checks to notice you even after that.

The drow cut of the same enchantment, black as the Underdark and twice as smug about it. It has the following Powers:

  • Invisibility I: While the hood is up, skip your Move to become Invisible until after you take an Action. Beings have Hinder on Checks to notice you even after that.

Wyrmdoom Crag's goliaths have kept this one in the main hall for generations. It has the following Powers:

  • (+1) Armor: +1 bonus to Armor while worn.
  • (+1) Protection: +1 bonus to all Saves while worn.

Nass Lantomir wanted one badly enough to die over it. It has the following Powers:

  • Scrying: Gaze into it to Scry on a Being or place you name, seeing and hearing it as though standing there. An unwilling Being resists with [Will], and knows it is being watched on a pass.
  • True-Seeing: While Scrying, the viewer sees through illusions, invisibility and disguises within the scried area.

A glass sphere the size of a fist that follows its owner around like a patient dog. It has the following Powers:

  • Radiant I: Speak the command word to make it shed sunlight out to Close, and again to douse it.
  • Levitation: The globe itself hovers, and follows within Close of whoever spoke the command word. It can be sent up to Far away and recalled.

A flawed yellow diamond with something restless behind the facets. It has the following Powers:

  • Summon Elemental: Shatter it to summon a friendly Earth Elemental for 1 Hour.

Netherese reading glasses, found in the captains' quarters of the Id Ascendant. It has the following Powers:

  • Minute Seeing: The wearer has Favor on Checks to examine anything within 1 foot.

A goliath peace offering, and a rather good messenger. It has the following Powers:

  • Silver Raven: Becomes a living silver raven for up to 12 Hours, then reverts and can't be used again until after a Rest. It can carry a message.

Pekoe Quint's, and it explains a great deal about Pekoe Quint. It has the following Powers:

  • Disguise: Cast Mirage on yourself at will to change your appearance. The illusion ends if the hat leaves your head.

Blowing it is always louder than anyone expects, including the person blowing it. It has the following Powers:

  • Thunderblast: Blow the horn to deal 5d6 damage in a Far Cone; those who fail [Endure] are also Dazed. On a roll of 1-4 on a d100, the horn explodes and is destroyed, dealing 10d6 to the user.

Drakareth wore it, and it is a large part of why Drakareth was a problem. It has the following Powers:

  • (+2) Protection: +2 bonus to Saves against Spells and other magical effects.
  • Resistance: Favor on Saves and damage reduction against magical damage.

Five beads on a chain, each one a small argument waiting to happen. It has the following Powers:

  • Fireball Beads: Detach a bead and throw it up to Far: it detonates for 3d6 Fire damage in a Near Sphere ([Reflex] to reduce). Multiple beads can be thrown at once, adding 1d6 each.

A fist-sized rock carved with an orcish eye, which watches back. It has the following Powers:

  • The Eyebiter's Shade: Once per Rest, summon the spirit of Vokarr the Eyebiter for 1 Hour. It answers questions about war and about orcs, and lies about everything else.

Sealed in an ancient tomb beneath Good Mead, alongside somebody who clearly wanted it kept there. It has the following Powers:

  • Recall: Once per Rest, regain Mana equal to a Spell you have already Cast.

Somewhere out in the ice, a construct is still waiting for whoever wears this. It has the following Powers:

  • Guardian Bond: The bonded Shield Guardian obeys your spoken commands, tries to stay within Far of you, and takes half of any damage dealt to you while it is within Close.
  • Telepathy: Telepathy (Far) with the bonded Shield Guardian only, which does not require Focus.

One ounce. There is no second ounce, and no known solvent short of Alkahest. It has the following Powers:

  • Sovereign Bond: Permanently bonds two objects. Only Alkahest will separate them.

A polished agate from the Chain Lightning Stadium, warm in the pocket. It has the following Powers:

  • (+1) Protection: +1 bonus to Saves and to all Checks.

A three-compartment quiver, each compartment far deeper than the outside of it suggests.

  • Holding 3: Occupies 1 Inventory Slot, but can hold 3 Slots of Items without counting against the carrier's Inventory Slots.

Salvage from the Id Ascendant. Nobody in Icewind Dale has the faintest idea what it is. It has the following Powers:

  • Energy Bolt: Requires a charged Energy Cell. Firing expends 1 of the cell's 5 charges, and no one in the Dale can refill it.

Two-handed, absurdly precise, and utterly unrepairable this side of the stars. It has the following Powers:

  • Energy Lance: Requires a charged Energy Cell. Firing expends 1 of the cell's 5 charges.

A flat crystalline wafer holding a charge that no Faerunian magic can replenish. It has the following Powers:

  • Charge Store: Holds 5 charges. Nothing in Faerun can refill it - once spent, it is inert forever.

Tali's thanks for dealing with the thing in the lake. It has the following Powers:

  • Inscribed Casting: Holds a single Casting of Beast, at the Rank it was scribed. Reading it aloud Casts the Spell without spending Mana and consumes the scroll.

How Nass Lantomir knew what she knew. It has the following Powers:

  • Inscribed Casting: Holds a single Casting of Guide, at the Rank it was scribed. Reading it aloud Casts the Spell without spending Mana and consumes the scroll.

Confiscated from Dzaan, and offered back as a reward. It has the following Powers:

  • Inscribed Casting: Holds a single Casting of Erupt, at the Rank it was scribed. Reading it aloud Casts the Spell without spending Mana and consumes the scroll.

Sealed in a chardalyn tube in the upside-down laboratory. It has the following Powers:

  • Inscribed Casting: Holds a single Casting of Fade, at the Rank it was scribed. Reading it aloud Casts the Spell without spending Mana and consumes the scroll.

Dropped down a waste chute, and none the worse for it. It has the following Powers:

  • Inscribed Casting: Holds a single Casting of Knock, at the Rank it was scribed. Reading it aloud Casts the Spell without spending Mana and consumes the scroll.

From an Icewind kobold shaman's tent. It has the following Powers:

  • Inscribed Casting: Holds a single Casting of Cure, at the Rank it was scribed. Reading it aloud Casts the Spell without spending Mana and consumes the scroll.

Found on the crowned rooftop of Grimskalle. It has the following Powers:

  • Inscribed Casting: Holds a single Casting of Cure, at the Rank it was scribed. Reading it aloud Casts the Spell without spending Mana and consumes the scroll.

Scrivenscry's way into Ythryn, and possibly yours out. It has the following Powers:

  • Inscribed Casting: Holds a single Casting of Portal, at the Rank it was scribed. Reading it aloud Casts the Spell without spending Mana and consumes the scroll.

Bundled with an archer figurine in the Dark Duchess's hold. It has the following Powers:

  • Inscribed Casting: Holds a single Casting of Dispel, at the Rank it was scribed. Reading it aloud Casts the Spell without spending Mana and consumes the scroll.

A cloudy green potion with a single seaweed frond drifting in it.

For 1 Hour, the consumer can breathe underwater. It does not grant a Swim speed.

The liquid shifts colour depending on which element it was brewed against.

For 1 Hour, the consumer gains Favor on Saves and damage reduction against one damage type, chosen when the potion is brewed.

Vagabond has no Radiant damage type, so Rime's potion of radiant resistance is brewed here as a warding draught against magical damage.

For 1 Hour, the consumer gains Favor on Saves and damage reduction against magical damage.

A clear red liquid that pulses gently, like something with a heartbeat.

The consumer's Fatigue is removed, and they regain the full benefit of a Rest. For the next 24 Hours they regain the maximum result on any healing die rolled for them.

Amber, with a swirl of gold that never settles.

The consumer's physical age is reduced by 1d6 + 6 years, to a minimum of 13. Each potion after the first carries a cumulative 10% chance of ageing them by the same amount instead.
